newsitem.title: INDIA: India cyclone toll climbs to 510.
newsitem.headline: India cyclone toll climbs to 510.

text.p: The death toll from the cyclone that struck India's southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh has reached 510, Hyderabad police officials said on Friday.

The cyclone struck the low-lying coastal strip south of Kakinada port late on Wednesday devastating the small farming communities in the fertile rice growing region of the Godavari river delta. "The death toll has risen to 510," a police official in Hyderabad, the state capital, told Reuters. He had no other details.

The state Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu flew over the flooded areas on Thursday and said the number of people killed could rise above 1,000. "The rice bowl of the state looks like a burial ground," he said.
Reddy Subramanium, a local tax collector from the town of Rajahmundry in East Godavari district, told Reuters the flood waters had receded but still covered low-lying areas.

He said several thousand head of cattle had been killed and around 250,000 hectares (625,000 acres) of rice paddy was inundated and 450,000 hectares (1.12 million acres) of other crops, including chilies, banana plantations and coconut groves were badly damaged.
H.S. Bramha, the official in coordinating relief operations from Hyderabad said about 150,000 houses, mainly mud-walled thatched dwellings had been destroyed or damaged.
